inline_comments.comment: This import crosses package boundaries via a deep relative path (`../../../../core/src/manager/utils/toHaveLiveRegion`), which violates the monorepo convention that requires inter-package imports to go through the public package export (e.g., `import { toHaveLiveRegion } from '@storybook/core/...'`). Deep relative paths are fragile under restructuring and bypass the package's intended API surface. The utility should either be exported from `@storybook/core`'s public exports map, or — since it is a test-only utility — moved into a `test-utils/` directory within the vitest addon itself so it does not need a cross-package import at all.

This test-only utility (a custom Vitest matcher) is placed under `core/src/manager/utils/`, which is production source. Per project convention, testing utilities must live under a dedicated `test-utils/` directory. Additionally, there is a path inconsistency: the existing type-augmentation files in this codebase (`code/core/vitest.d.ts`, `code/addons/vitest/src/custom-matchers.d.ts`) declare `toHaveLiveRegion` by importing from `./core/src/shared/utils/toHaveLiveRegion`, but this diff places the file at `manager/utils/`. If those augmentation files are not updated to point to the new path, the type declarations will not resolve and TypeScript will still error on `expect(x).toHaveLiveRegion(...)` calls.

The file exports the matcher function but contains no TypeScript module augmentation. Without a `declare module 'vitest' { interface Assertion<T> { toHaveLiveRegion(options: LiveRegionMatcherOptions): T } }` block (or the equivalent for `storybook/test`), every call site — `expect(container).toHaveLiveRegion(...)` in both the test file and the stories — will produce a TypeScript compile error because the method is unknown on the `Assertion` type. The established pattern in this repo is to add such declarations to `code/core/vitest.d.ts` (for Vitest) and/or a `custom-matchers.d.ts` alongside the consuming package. The diff does not include changes to any `.d.ts` file, so this is missing.

The `as any` type assertion here works around the mock's strict typing. Per project convention, when suppressing a TypeScript error caused by overly strict types, prefer `// @ts-expect-error` with an explanatory comment over a type assertion (`as any`). `@ts-expect-error` fails the build if the error it suppresses disappears (keeping suppressions honest), while `as any` silently survives even after the underlying type is fixed. The existing `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` comment should also be replaced with the TypeScript suppression.

The play function only asserts that the expected announcement IS present but does not assert that unexpected announcements are NOT present. For example, it verifies `'Test run started.'` is announced, but does not verify that `'Test run crashed.'` or `'Test run finished.'` were not. Per project convention, play functions should combine a positive assertion with a negative assertion (e.g., add `expect(document.body).not.toHaveLiveRegion({ text: /Test run finished/ })`) to prevent false positives where stale state from a prior story could satisfy only the positive check. The same gap applies to `AnnouncesTestRunFinished` (line 388) and `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed` (line 421).

None of the three new stories (`AnnouncesTestRunStart`, `AnnouncesTestRunFinished`, `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed`) include a `tags` property, yet the PR description explicitly states they are "Tagged with `vitest` for vitest-only test execution." Without `tags: ['vitest']`, these stories will run in all test environments (including Chromatic, browser mode, etc.), not just Vitest. If the intent is to confine them to Vitest, add `tags: ['vitest']` to each story definition.

general_comments.comment: The announcement assertions in all three play functions use a DOM-scan approach (`toHaveLiveRegion` inspects live-region element text content). This is inherently racy: `@react-aria/live-announcer` sets the text of an ARIA live region node and then clears it after a short delay (~500 ms). The `waitFor` retry window must catch the announcement before the clearance fires, making these tests potentially flaky under load or in slow CI environments. The PR description originally proposed using `extend-to-be-announced`, which intercepts `announce()` calls at the library level (timing-independent), but that library does not appear anywhere in the diff. A more reliable alternative is to spy on the `announce` function directly with `vi.spyOn` (capturing the call synchronously) rather than scanning the DOM for ephemeral text nodes.
